content: 1. Ofloxacin and calcium citrate can mutually reduce each other's levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal (GI) absorption. This interaction is specific to the oral forms of both agents. It is recommended to use caution, monitor the patient, and separate administration by at least 2 hours. 2. Ofloxacin and calcium gluconate can also reduce each other's levels via inhibition of GI absorption. This interaction applies only to their oral forms. Caution and monitoring are advised, with a 2-hour separation between doses. 3. Chlorpromazine and ofloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is necessary. 4. Ofloxacin and citalopram both increase the QTc interval. Caution is advised, and ECG monitoring is recommended, especially when co-administered with other QT-prolonging drugs. 5. Clarithromycin and ofloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 6. Clomipramine and ofloxacin both increase the QTc interval. Therapy should be adjusted, and close monitoring is necessary. 7. Clozapine and ofloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are advised. 8. Ofloxacin can decrease the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are recommended. 9. Co-administration of quinolone antibiotics, such as ofloxacin, with corticosteroids (e.g., corticotropin, cortisone, dexamethasone, hydrocortisone) may increase the risk of tendon rupture. Caution and monitoring are advised. 10. Crizotinib and ofloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. ECG monitoring and caution are recommended. 11. Dasatinib and ofloxacin both increase the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are advised. 12. Degarelix and ofloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 13. Desipramine and ofloxacin both increase the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is necessary. 14. Deutetrabenazine and ofloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are advised. At the maximum recommended dose, deutetrabenazine does not clinically prolong the QT interval significantly. However, certain conditions may increase the risk of torsades de pointes or sudden death when combined with QT-prolonging drugs. 15. Ofloxacin can decrease the levels or effects of dienogest/estradiol valerate by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are recommended. Alternative or additional forms of birth control may be advisable during concurrent use. 16. Ofloxacin can increase the levels or effects of digoxin by altering intestinal flora. Conversely, digoxin can increase the levels or effects of ofloxacin due to competition for renal tubular clearance. Caution and monitoring are advised. 17. Dofetilide and ofloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is necessary. 18. Dolasetron and ofloxacin both increase the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 19. Donepezil and ofloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are advised. 20. Doxepin and ofloxacin both increase the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is necessary. 21. Dronedarone and ofloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is necessary. 22. Droperidol and ofloxacin both increase the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is necessary. 23. Efavirenz and ofloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 24. Eliglustat and ofloxacin both increase the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are advised. 25. Epinephrine and ofloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is necessary. 26. Erythromycin (base, ethylsuccinate, lactobionate, stearate) and ofloxacin all increase the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is necessary. 27. Escitalopram increases the toxicity of ofloxacin by prolonging the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 28. Ofloxacin can decrease the levels or effects of estradiol, estrogens (conjugated synthetic), estropipate, ethinyl estradiol, and mestranol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are recommended. 29. Ofloxacin decreases the effects of ethotoin and fosphenytoin by unknown mechanisms. Caution and monitoring are advised. There are also case reports of quinolones increasing phenytoin levels. 30. Etrasimod and ofloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is necessary. Etrasimod may transiently decrease heart rate and delay AV conduction, increasing the risk of QT prolongation and torsades de pointes when combined with QT-prolonging drugs. 31. Ezogabine and ofloxacin both increase each other's toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Slight and transient QT prolongation has been observed with ezogabine, particularly at high doses. 32. Fennel decreases the levels of ofloxacin by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Caution and monitoring are advised. 33. Ferric citrate decreases the levels or effects of ofloxacin by drug binding in the GI tract. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Administer at least 2 hours before or after ferric citrate. 34. Fingolimod and ofloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are advised. 35. Flecainide and ofloxacin both increase the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 36. Fluconazole and ofloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is necessary. 37. Fludrocortisone and ofloxacin both increase the risk of tendon rupture when co-administered. Caution and monitoring are advised. 38. Fluoxetine and ofloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 39. Fluphenazine and ofloxacin both increase the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is necessary. 40. Fluvoxamine and ofloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is necessary. 41. Formoterol and ofloxacin both increase the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is necessary. 42. Foscarnet and ofloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 43. Ofloxacin and fostemsavir both increase the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are advised. QT prolongation has been reported with higher-than-recommended doses of fostemsavir. 44. Ofloxacin and gemtuzumab both prolong the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 45. Gepirone and ofloxacin both increase the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is necessary. 46. Gilteritinib and ofloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are advised. 47. Ofloxacin increases the effects of glimepiride, glipizide, and glyburide by pharmacodynamic synergism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Quinolone antibiotics may cause hyperor hypoglycemia, with gatifloxacin being the most likely to cause dysglycemia and moxifloxacin the least likely. 48. Goserelin increases the toxicity of ofloxacin by prolonging the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are recommended, as this increases the risk of torsades de pointes. 49. Granisetron and ofloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are advised. 50. Haloperidol and ofloxacin both increase the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is necessary. 51. Histrelin increases the toxicity of ofloxacin by prolonging the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are recommended, as this increases the risk of torsades de pointes. 52. Hydrocortisone and ofloxacin both increase the risk of tendon rupture when co-administered. Caution and monitoring are advised. 53. Hydroxyzine and ofloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 54. Ofloxacin and ibuprofen IV may increase the risk of CNS stimulation or seizures due to displacement of GABA from brain receptors. Caution and monitoring are advised. 55. Iloperidone and ofloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 56. Imipramine and ofloxacin both increase the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is necessary. 57. Indacaterol (inhaled) and ofloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are recommended, as QT-prolonging drugs may increase the risk of ventricular arrhythmias. 58. Ofloxacin increases the effects of various forms of insulin (e.g., aspart, detemir, glargine, glulisine, lispro, NPH, regular human) by pharmacodynamic synergism. Caution and monitoring are recommended, as quinolone antibiotics may cause hyperor hypoglycemia. 59. Itraconazole and ofloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is necessary. 60. Ketoconazole and ofloxacin both increase the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is necessary. 61. Lanthanum carbonate decreases the levels of ofloxacin by cation binding in the GI tract. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Administer oral quinolones at least 1 hour before or 4 hours after lanthanum. 62. Lapatinib and ofloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are advised. 63. Ofloxacin and lenvatinib both increase the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Lenvatinib prescribing information advises close ECG monitoring when co-administered with QT-prolonging drugs. 64. Leuprolide increases the toxicity of ofloxacin by prolonging the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are recommended, as this increases the risk of torsades de pointes. 65. Levofloxacin and ofloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are advised. 66. Levoketoconazole and ofloxacin both increase the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is necessary. 67. Ofloxacin decreases the levels or effects of levonorgestrel/ethinyl estradiol/ferrous bisglycinate by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are recommended. Antibiotics may decrease hormonal contraceptive efficacy. 68. Lithium and ofloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are advised. 69. Lofepramine and ofloxacin both increase the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is necessary. 70. Lumefantrine and ofloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is necessary. 71. Magnesium salts (e.g., chloride, citrate, hydroxide, oxide, sulfate) decrease the levels of ofloxacin by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Caution and monitoring are recommended, with a 2-hour separation between doses. 72. Maprotiline and ofloxacin both increase the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is necessary. 73. Mavorixafor and ofloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is necessary. Mavorixafor causes concentration-dependent QTc prolongation, and dose reduction or discontinuation may be required in patients with risk factors for QTc prolongation.
